With the authorization of the Colombian government and the participation of the [[International Red Cross]], a Venezuelan helicopter transported them to [[Caracas]] from [[San José del Guaviare]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/02/27/colombia.hostage/ |title=Colombian rebels free 4 hostages |work=CNN |date=27 February 2008 |access-date=22 May 2010 |archive-date=25 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090425121907/http://www.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/02/27/colombia.hostage/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The FARC–EP had called its planned release of the hostages a gesture of recognition for the mediation efforts of Chávez, who had called on the international community to recognize the rebels as [[belligerents]] a month prior.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/2008/02/27/america/colombia.php |title=Colombian rebels release 4 hostages |date=27 February 2008 |work=International Herald Tribune |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080314221256/http://www.iht.com/articles/2008/02/27/america/colombia.php |archive-date=14 March 2008}}</ref> Colombian President [[Álvaro Uribe]], who had tense relations with Chávez, thanked the socialist leader and called for the release of all hostages. He said Colombia was still in a fight "against terrorist actions" but was open to reconciliation.{{Citation needed|date=February 2010}}

==== Anti-FARC rallies ====
[[File:Logo web.jpg|thumb|300px|Banner of the February 2008 anti-FARC rallies with slogans in Spanish, English, Dutch, and French. In the French version "contre la torture" and "contre la guerre" mean "against torture" and "against the war" respectively.<ref name="movements.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.movements.org/case-study/entry/oscar-morales-and-one-million-voices-against-farc/ |title=Oscar Morales and One Million Voices Against FARC |work=Movements.org |date=23 July 2010 |access-date=1 April 2013 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022220325/http://www.movements.org/case-study/entry/oscar-morales-and-one-million-voices-against-farc/ |archive-date=22 October 2013}}</ref><ref name="bushcenter.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.bushcenter.org/blog/2012/09/13/one-million-voices-against-farc-milestone-freedom |title=One Million Voices Against the FARC: A Milestone for Freedom |work=BushCenter.org |date=4 February 2011 |access-date=1 April 2013 |archive-date=11 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111062016/http://www.bushcenter.org/blog/2012/09/13/one-million-voices-against-farc-milestone-freedom |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="millondevoces.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.millondevoces.org/contenido/ |title=One Million Voices Against FARC |work=millondevoces.org |language=es |access-date=1 April 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323095958/http://www.millondevoces.org/contenido/ |archive-date=23 March 2013}}</ref>]]
On 4 February 2008, anti-FARC protests were held in 45 Colombian cities and towns, with an estimated 1.5&nbsp;million people coming out in Bogotá alone. Solidarity rallies were held in some 200 cities worldwide including Berlin, Barcelona, London, Madrid, Toronto, Dubai, Miami, New York, Brisbane, and La Paz.<ref name="movements.org"/><ref name="bushcenter.org"/><ref name="millondevoces.org"/> The protests were originally organised through Facebook and were also supported by local Colombian media outlets as well as the Colombian government. Participation estimates vary from the hundreds of thousands to several millions of people in Colombia and thousands worldwide.<ref name="BBCFeb4">{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/7225824.stm |title=Colombians in huge FARC protest |date=4 February 2008 |website=BBC News |access-date=6 January 2010}}</ref><ref name="WashingtonPostFeb4">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/02/04/AR2008020403019.html |title=Anti-FARC Rallies Held Worldwide |date=5 February 2008 |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=7 February 2008 |archive-date=9 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109163323/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/02/04/AR2008020403019.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ReutersFeb4">{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN0459656620080205 |title=Colombians take to streets in huge anti-FARC march |date=5 February 2008 |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=24 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100124115551/http://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN0459656620080205 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="SMHFeb4">{{cite news |url=https://www.smh.com.au/news/world/worldwide-protests-against-colombian-kidnapping/2008/02/05/1202090388923.html |title=Worldwide protests against Colombian kidnapping |date=5 February 2008 |newspaper=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=5 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605071345/http://www.smh.com.au/news/world/worldwide-protests-against-colombian-kidnapping/2008/02/05/1202090388923.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="msnbcFeb4">{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna22998957 |title=Millions of Colombians march against rebels |date=4 February 2008 |website=[[NBC News]] |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=16 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016031717/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/22998957/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Shortly before the rallies took place 13 demobilised [[United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia|AUC]] paramilitary leaders, including [[Salvatore Mancuso]], had expressed their support of the protest through a communique. However, this move was rejected by organiser [[Carlos Andrés Santiago]], who stated that such an endorsement was harmful and criticised the AUC's actions.<ref name="AUCrejection">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.semana.com/wf_InfoArticulo.aspx?IdArt=109143 |title=Organizadores de la marcha rechazan el apoyo de Salvatore Mancuso |date=1 February 2008 |magazine=[[Revista Semana]] |language=es |access-date=3 January 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080408013243/http://www.semana.com/wf_InfoArticulo.aspx?idArt=109143 |archive-date=8 April 2008}}</ref>

On 20 July 2008, a subsequent set of rallies against FARC included thousands of Colombians in Bogotá and hundreds of thousands throughout the rest of the country.<ref name="BBCJuly20">{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7516533.stm |title=Colombian anti-FARC rally |date=20 July 2008 |website=BBC News |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=22 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100122134052/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7516533.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="AJJuly20">{{cite web |url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2008/07/20087201614073667.html |title=Colombians hold anti-FARC rally |date=20 July 2008 |website=Al Jazeera English |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=13 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081213072748/http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2008/07/20087201614073667.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Deaths of Raúl Reyes and Manuel Marulanda Vélez ====
{{Main|2008 Andean diplomatic crisis}}
[[File:Raulreyesfarc.png|thumb|left|130px|[[Raúl Reyes]]]]
On 1 March 2008, Raul Reyes, a member of FARC's ruling Secretariat, was killed just across the border from Colombia, in the small village of Santa Rosa, Ecuador, after Colombian planes bombarded a FARC camp there. The bombardment was "followed by troops in helicopters who recovered the bodies of Reyes and another 16 rebels." Reyes was the former FARC chief negotiator during the unsuccessful 1998–2002 peace process, and was also a key FARC hostage release negotiator. Reyes' demise marked the first time that a FARC Secretariat member had been killed in combat.<ref name="bbc2"/>

This incident led to a breakdown in diplomatic relations between Ecuador and Colombia, and between Venezuela and Colombia.<ref name="bbc2">{{cite news |last=McDermott |first=Jeremy |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7273320.stm |title=FARC aura of invincibility shattered |work=BBC News |date=1 March 2008 |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-date=5 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080305005015/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7273320.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://edition.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/03/02/chavez.colombia/index.html |title=Chavez orders troops to Colombia border |work=CNN |date=2 March 2008 |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-date=19 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111119044745/http://edition.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/03/02/chavez.colombia/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Ecuador condemned the attack.<ref>{{Cite news |title=War of words opens LatAm summit |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7283151.stm |work=BBC News |date=2008-03-07 |access-date=2016-02-08 |archive-date=7 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307143837/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/7283151.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ecuador officially condemns Santos and Sanin stance on cross-border attacks |url=http://colombiareports.com/ecuador-officially-condemns-santos-and-sanin-stance-on-cross-border-attacks/ |first=Camilla |last=Pease-Watkin |website=Colombia Reports |access-date=2016-02-08 |date=2010-04-28 |archive-date=13 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113082914/http://colombiareports.com/ecuador-officially-condemns-santos-and-sanin-stance-on-cross-border-attacks/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The incident also resulted in diplomatic strains between the United States and Ecuador, following revelations that the [[Central Intelligence Agency]] provided intelligence that allowed the Colombian military to locate the FARC–EP commander and ordnance used in the attack.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ecuador: Report Says U.S. Aided Attack on Rebels |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/12/11/world/americas/11briefs-EcuadorBrf.html |newspaper=The New York Times |date=2009-12-10 |access-date=2016-02-08 |issn=0362-4331 |first=Simon |last=Romero |archive-date=13 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113151316/http://www.nytimes.com/2009/12/11/world/americas/11briefs-EcuadorBrf.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Covert action in Colombia |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/investigative/2013/12/21/covert-action-in-colombia/ |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=2016-02-08 |first=Dana |last=Priest |archive-date=30 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830153417/http://www.washingtonpost.com/sf/investigative/2013/12/21/covert-action-in-colombia/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Phone led US experts to FARC leader Raul Reyes |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/1581212/Phone-led-US-experts-to-Farc-leader-Raul-Reyes.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/1581212/Phone-led-US-experts-to-Farc-leader-Raul-Reyes.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=2016-02-08 |first1=Bill |last1=Lowther |first2=Philip |last2=Sherwell |date=2008-03-09}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

It has been considered the biggest blow against FARC–EP in its more than four decades of existence.<ref name="bbc2"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/conflicto/noticias/ARTICULO-WEB-NOTA_INTERIOR-3981514.html |title=Colombia dice que no violó soberanía de Ecuador en operativo que llevó a la muerte de Raúl Reyes |date=3 March 2008 |work=El Tiempo |language=es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080611114929/http://www.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/03/07/colombia.farc/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 June 2008 |access-date=2 March 2008}}</ref> This event was quickly followed by the death of [[Iván Ríos]], another member of FARC–EP's seven-man Secretariat, less than a week later, by the hand of his own bodyguard. It came as a result of heavy Colombian military pressure and a reward offer of up to $5&nbsp;million from the Colombian government.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/03/07/colombia.farc/index.html |title=Second Colombian rebel leader killed |date=7 March 2008 |work=CNN |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080808141947/http://www.cnn.com/2008/WORLD/americas/03/07/colombia.farc/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 August 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2001.com.ve/noticias_2001online.asp?registro=89073&visit=261&act=1 |title=Guerrillero cuenta porqué mató y cortó la mano a jefe FARC |work=2001.com.ve |access-date=17 October 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928032732/http://www.2001.com.ve/noticias_2001online.asp?registro=89073&visit=261&act=1 |archive-date=28 September 2011}}</ref>

After the attack, the Colombian military forces managed to secure six laptop computers belonging to Reyes, in which they found information linking several left-wing Colombian personalities, such as politicians, journalists and human rights activists with terrorist activities.

Manuel Marulanda Vélez died on 26 March 2008 after a heart attack. His death would be kept a secret, until Colombian magazine ''[[Semana]]'' published an interview with Colombian defence minister [[Juan Manuel Santos]] on 24 May 2008 in which Santos mentions the death of [[Manuel Marulanda Vélez]]. The news was confirmed by FARC–EP commander [[Timoleón Jiménez|Timochenko]] on Latin American television station [[teleSUR]] on 25 May 2008. Timochenko announced the new commander in chief was [[Alfonso Cano]]<ref>{{cite news |url=https://colombiareports.com/farc-admits-death-of-manuel-marandula/ |title=FARC confirm death of 'Manuel Marulanda' |first=Adriaan |last=Alsema |date=25 May 2008 |work=Colombia Reports |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806175719/https://colombiareports.com/farc-admits-death-of-manuel-marandula/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After speculations in several national and international media about the "softening up" of the FARC and the announcement of Colombian President Álvaro Uribe that several FARC leaders were ready to surrender and free their captives, the secretariat of the FARC sent out a [[communiqué]] emphasizing the death of their founder would not change their approach towards the captives or the humanitarian agreement.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://colombiareports.com/farc-death-marulanda-doesnt-change-anything/ |title=FARC: death Marulanda doesn't change anything |date=27 May 2008 |work=Colombia Reports |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806155832/https://colombiareports.com/farc-death-marulanda-doesnt-change-anything/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://bolivarsomostodos.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=266&Itemid=37 |title=Comandante Manuel Marulanda Vélez: ¡Juramos vencer! |date=25 May 2008 |work=FARC |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081211194402/http://bolivarsomostodos.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=266&Itemid=37 |archive-date=11 December 2008}}</ref>

==== Late-2008 prisoner events ====
On 11 January 2008 during the annual State of the Nation in the [[Venezuelan National Assembly]], Venezuelan President Hugo Chávez referred to the FARC as "a real army that occupies territory in Colombia, they're not terrorists&nbsp;... They have a political goal and we have to recognise that".<ref name="bloomberg">{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=newsarchive&sid=aMaO2D0fSyH4 |title=Chavez Calls FARC a 'Real Army' Worthy of Respect |work=Bloomberg |access-date=11 January 2014 |date=11 January 2008 |archive-date=12 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112015856/http://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=newsarchive&sid=aMaO2D0fSyH4 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, on 13 January 2008, Chávez stated his disapproval of the FARC–EP strategy of armed struggle and kidnapping, saying "I don't agree with kidnapping and I don't agree with armed struggle".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/worldNews/idUSN1336689820080113 |title=Hugo Chavez tells Colombian rebels to stop kidnapping |date=13 January 2008 |work=Reuters |access-date=1 July 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210042402/http://www.reuters.com/article/worldNews/idUSN1336689820080113 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 7 March at the Cumbre de Rio, Chávez stated again that the FARC–EP should lay down their arms "Look at what has happened and is happening in Latin America, reflect on this (FARC–EP), we are done with war&nbsp;... enough with all this death".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gz57qB9_1bs |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211103/Gz57qB9_1bs| archive-date=2021-11-03 |url-status=live|title=Hugo Chavez en la Cumbre del Grupo Río 4ta parte |work=YouTube |date=7 March 2008 |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref>{{primary source inline|date=June 2022}} On 8 June Chavez repeated his call for a political solution and an end to the war, "The guerrilla war is history&nbsp;... At this moment in Latin America, an armed guerrilla movement is out of place".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/chavez-calls-on-colombian-rebels-to-end-struggle-free-hostages |work=Fox News |title=Chavez Calls on Colombian Rebels to End Struggle, Free Hostages |date=9 June 2008 |access-date=8 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090211083824/http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,364368,00.html |archive-date=11 February 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 2 July 2008, under a Colombian military operation called [[Operation Jaque]], the FARC–EP was tricked by the Colombian Government into releasing 15 captives to Colombian Intelligence agents disguised as journalists and international aid workers in a helicopter rescue. Military intelligence agents infiltrated the guerrilla ranks and led the local commander in charge of the captives, [[Gerardo Aguilar Ramírez]], alias Cesar, to believe they were going to take them by helicopter to Alfonso Cano, the guerrillas' supreme leader. The rescued included [[Íngrid Betancourt]] (former presidential candidate), U.S. military contractors [[Marc Gonsalves]], [[Thomas Howes (hostage)|Thomas Howes]], and [[Keith Stansell]], as well as eleven Colombian police officers and soldiers. The commander, Cesar and one other rebel were taken into custody by agents without incident after boarding the helicopter.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/politician-ingrid-betancourt-3-american-hostages-rescued-from-colombian-rebels |title=Politician Ingrid Betancourt, 3 American Hostages Rescued From Colombian Rebels |work=Fox News |date=2 July 2008 |access-date=3 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080704034837/http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,375481,00.html |archive-date=4 July 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 4 July, some observers questioned whether or not this was an intercepted captive release made to look like a rescue.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/us_and_americas/article4270908.ece |title=Brilliant or a sham? Questions asked over Ingrid Betancourt rescue |work=The Times |location=London |first1=Thomas |last1=Catan |first2=Charles |last2=Bremner |date=4 July 2008 |access-date=22 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081006102338/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/news/world/us_and_americas/article4270908.ece |archive-date=6 October 2008}}</ref> In a 5 July communique, FARC itself blamed rebels Cesar and Enrique for the escape of the captives and acknowledged the event as a setback but reiterated their willingness to reach future humanitarian agreements.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cedema.org/ver.php?id=2712 |title=Despejando las mentiras acerca de la fuga de los 15 prisioneros de guerra |work=Cedema |date=5 July 2008 |language=es |access-date=6 January 2010 |archive-date=13 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100613181342/http://cedema.org/ver.php?id=2712 |url-status=live }}</ref> Immediately after the captive rescue, Colombian military forces cornered the rest of FARC–EP's 1st Front, the unit which had held the captives. Colombian forces did not wish to attack the 1st Front but instead offered them amnesty if they surrender.<ref>{{cite news |title=A Smarter Way To Fight |first=Michael |last=Hirsh |date=21 July 2008 |newspaper=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref> Colombia's Program for Humanitarian Attention for the Demobilized announced in August 2008 that 339 members of Colombia's rebel groups surrendered and handed in their weapons in July, including 282 guerrillas from the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://colombiareports.com/2008/08/13/over-300-guerrillas-surrendered-weapons-in-july/ |title=Over 300 Guerrillas surrendered weapons in July |date=13 August 2008 |work=Colombia Reports |access-date=30 August 2008}} {{dead link|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

[[Óscar Tulio Lizcano]], a [[Colombian Conservative Party]] congressman, was kidnapped 5 August 2000. On Sunday, 26 October 2008, the ex-congressman escaped from FARC–EP rebels. Tulio Lizcano was a [[hostage]] for over eight years, and escaped with a FARC–EP rebel he convinced to travel with him. They evaded pursuit for three days as they trekked through mountains and forests, encountering the military in the western coastal region of Colombia. Tulio Lizcano is the first hostage to escape since the successful military rescue of Íngrid Betancourt, and the longest-held political hostage by the organization. He became the 22nd Colombian political hostage to gain freedom during 2008.{{Citation needed|date=February 2010}}

During his final days in captivity, Lizcano told Santos, they had nothing to eat but wild palm hearts and [[sugar cane]]. With the military tightening the noose, a FARC–EP rebel turned himself in and provided Colombian authorities with Lizcano's exact location in the northwest state of [[Department of Chocó|Choco]]. As police and army troops prepared to launch a rescue operation, Lizcano escaped alongside one of his guerrilla guards who had decided to desert. The two men hiked through the rain forest for three days and nights until they encountered an army patrol.<ref name="chron.com">{{cite news |url=https://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/world/6079567.html |title=Captor helps hostage in Colombia escape after 8 years |work=Houston Chronicle |first=John |last=Otis |date=26 October 2008 |access-date=17 April 2020 |archive-date=29 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629131956/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/world/6079567.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Speaking from a clinic in the western city of Cali, Mr Lizcano said that when soldiers saw him screaming from across a jungle river, they thought he was drunk and ignored him. Only when he lifted the FARC–EP rebel's Galil assault rifle did the soldiers begin to understand that he was escaping from the FARC–EP rebels. "They jumped into the river, and then I started to shout, 'I'm Lizcano'", he said.<ref name="chron.com"/>

Soon after the liberation of this prominent political hostage, the [[Vice President of Colombia]] [[Francisco Santos Calderón]] called Latin America's biggest guerrilla group a "[[paper tiger]]" with little control of the nation's territory, adding that "they have really been diminished to the point where we can say they are a minimal threat to Colombian security", and that "After six years of going after them, reducing their income and promoting reinsertion of most of their members, they look like a paper tiger." However, he warned against any kind of premature triumphalism, because "crushing the rebels will take time". The {{convert|500000|km2|sp=us}} of jungle in Colombia makes it hard to track them down to fight.<ref name="bloomberg.com">{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601086&sid=aCsN3xsYNI0M&refer=latin_america |title=FARC Is a 'Paper Tiger' After Offensive, Desertions |work=Bloomberg |date=29 October 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090626150025/http://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601086&sid=aCsN3xsYNI0M&refer=latin_america |archive-date=26 June 2009}}</ref>

==== 2009 prisoner events ====
On 21 December 2008, The FARC–EP announced that they would release civilian hostages [[Alan Jara]], [[Sigifredo López]], three low-ranking police officers and a low-ranking soldier to Senator [[Piedad Córdoba]] as a humanitarian gesture.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caracol.com.co/nota.aspx?id=734801 |title=Las FARC anuncian la liberación de seis, pero secuestran a otros diez |work=Caracol Radio |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |date=2008-12-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728092539/http://www.caracol.com.co/nota.aspx?id=734801 |archive-date=28 July 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 1 February 2009, the FARC–EP proceeded with the release of the four security force members, Juan Fernando Galicio Uribe, José Walter Lozano Guarnizo, Alexis Torres Zapata and William Giovanni Domínguez Castro. All of them were captured in 2007. Jara (kidnapped in 2001) was released on 3 February and López (kidnapped in 2002) was released on 5 February.

On 17 March 2009, The FARC–EP released Swedish hostage Erik Roland Larsson. Larsson, paralyzed in half his body, was handed over to detectives in a rugged region of the northern state of Córdoba. Larsson was kidnapped from his ranch in Tierralta, not far from where he was freed, on 16 May 2007, along with his Colombian girlfriend, Diana Patricia Pena while paying workers. She escaped that same month following a gun battle between her captors and police. Larsson suffered a stroke while in captivity. The FARC–EP had sought a $5&nbsp;million ransom. One of Larsson's sons said that the ransom was not paid.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2009/mar/18/farc-hostage-release-larsson |location=London |work=The Guardian |first=Rory |last=McCarthy |title=Colombian FARC rebels release last known foreign hostage |date=18 March 2009}}</ref>

On 22 December 2009, the body of [[Luis Francisco Cuéllar]], the Governor of [[Caquetá Department|Caquetá]], was discovered, a day after he had been kidnapped from his house in [[Florencia, Caquetá]]. Officials said the abduction and execution had been carried by the FARC. According to officials, he had been killed soon after the abduction. The kidnappers cut the governor's throat as they evaded security forces. In a statement broadcast on radio, the acting governor, Patricia Vega, said, "I no longer have any doubts that FARC has done it again." The FARC claimed responsibility for Cuéllar's kidnapping and murder in January 2010. The group said that they kidnapped him in order to "put him on trial for corruption" and blamed his death on an attempt to rescue him by force.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN05122506 |title=Colombian rebels say killed governor, blame Uribe |first=Hugh |last=Bronstein |date=6 January 2010 |work=Reuters |access-date=1 July 2017 |archive-date=17 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170617095256/http://www.reuters.com/article/idUSN05122506 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8427582.stm |title=Kidnapped Colombian governor found with throat slit |date=23 December 2009 |work=BBC News |access-date=23 December 2009 |archive-date=23 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091223052144/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8427582.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 16 April 2009, the FARC–EP announced that they would release Army Corporal [[Pablo Emilio Moncayo]] Cabrera to Piedad Córdoba as a humanitarian gesture. Moncayo was kidnapped on 21 December 1997. On 28 June 2009, the FARC announced that they would release soldier Josue Daniel Calvo Sanchez. Calvo was kidnapped on 20 April 2009. Calvo was released on 28 March 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8591334.stm |title=FARC rebels poised to free Colombian soldier |website=BBC News |language=en-GB |access-date=2017-01-25 |date=2010-03-28 |archive-date=2 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202181323/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8591334.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Moncayo was released on 30 March 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8595140.stm |title=Colombia FARC rebels release hostage Pablo Moncayo |website=BBC News |language=en-GB |access-date=2017-01-25 |date=2010-03-31 |archive-date=9 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109043108/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/8595140.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 13 June 2010, Colombian troops rescued Police Colonel Luis Herlindo Mendieta Ovalle, Police Captain Enrique Murillo Sanchez and Army Sergeant Arbey Delgado Argote in an event known as Operation Chameleon, twelve years after the individuals were captured; Argote was kidnapped on 3 August 1998. Ovalle and Sanchez were kidnapped on 1 November 1998. On 14 June, Police Lieutenant William Donato Gomez was also rescued. He was also kidnapped on 3 August 1998.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.smh.com.au/breaking-news-world/colombia-rescues-police-held-for-12-years-by-farc-20100614-y8n7.html |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |first=Pablo |last=Rodriguez |title=Colombia rescues police held for 12 years by FARC |date=14 June 2010}}</ref>

=== Santos presidency (2010–2018) ===
==== 2010–2011: Increased violence ====
{{See also|List of attacks attributed to FARC}}
President [[Juan Manuel Santos]] began his term with a suspected FARC bomb-blast in Bogotá.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-10953545 |title=Car bomb rocks Colombian capital |date=12 August 2010 |website=BBC News |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=9 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109031522/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-10953545 |url-status=live }}</ref> This followed the resolution of the [[2010 Colombia–Venezuela diplomatic crisis]] which erupted over outgoing President [[Álvaro Uribe]]'s allegations of active Venezuelan support for FARC.

In early September 2010, FARC–EP attacks in the [[Nariño Department]] and [[Putumayo Department]] in southern Colombia killed some fifty policemen and soldiers in hit-and-run assaults.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://af.reuters.com/article/energyOilNews/idAFN1025921520100910 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119130307/http://af.reuters.com/article/energyOilNews/idAFN1025921520100910 |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 January 2012 |title=Colombian rebel attacks intensify, dozens killed |date=10 September 2010 |website=[[Reuters]] |access-date=18 May 2020}}</ref>

According to a December report by the [[Corporación Nuevo Arco Iris]] NGO, 473 FARC–EP guerrillas and 357 members of the Colombian security forces died in combat between January and September 2010. An additional 1,382 government soldiers or policemen were wounded during the same period, with the report estimating that the total number of casualties could reach 2,500 by the end of the year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://colombiareports.com/death-of-mono-jojoy-forces-farc-to-carry-out-different-strategy-ngo/ |title=Death of Mono Jojoy forces FARC to carry out different strategy: NGO |first=Adriaan |last=Alsema |date=1 December 2010 |website=Colombia Reports |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806214404/https://colombiareports.com/death-of-mono-jojoy-forces-farc-to-carry-out-different-strategy-ngo/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Nuevo Arco Iris head [[León Valencia]] considered that FARC guerrillas have reacted to a series of successful military blows against them by splitting up their forces into smaller groups and intensifying the offensive use of anti-personnel [[land mine]]s, leading to what he called a further "degradation" of the conflict. Valencia also added that both coca crops and the drug trade have "doubled" in areas with FARC–EP presence. Researcher Claudia López considered that the Colombian government is winning the strategic and aerial side of the war but not the infantry front, where both the FARC–EP and ELN continue to maintain an offensive capacity.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jGjA2qhxBW103DTvIMiF7ebHyNMw?docId=CNG.c83e4798ef35929e6b470b886e11dd0f.481 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120523004256/http://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5jGjA2qhxBW103DTvIMiF7ebHyNMw?docId=CNG.c83e4798ef35929e6b470b886e11dd0f.481 |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 May 2012 |title=Colombianas FARC resisten con nueva estrategia tras duros golpes sufridos |date=1 December 2010 |website=AFP |via=Google News |language=es}}</ref>

The [[International Crisis Group]] claimed that the military offensives carried out under former President Álvaro Uribe and President [[Juan Manuel Santos]] had led to the number of FARC-EC combatants being reduced to around 7,000, less than half the 20,000 combatants estimated to have been employed by the FARC-EC in the early 2000s. The same organization also stated that the military offensive had been able to reduce FARC territorial control and push [[guerilla]]s to more remote and sparsely populated regions, often close to territorial or internal borders.<ref name="CrisisGroup.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.crisisgroup.org/~/media/Files/latin-america/colombia/053-the-day-after-tomorrow-colombia-s-farc-and-the-end-of-the-conflict.pdf |title=The Day After Tomorrow: Colombia's FARC and the End of the Conflict |date=11 December 2014 |website=[[International Crisis Group]] |access-date=11 December 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213013210/http://www.crisisgroup.org/~/media/Files/latin-america/colombia/053-the-day-after-tomorrow-colombia-s-farc-and-the-end-of-the-conflict.pdf |archive-date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

Colombian authorities announced the death of [[Víctor Julio Suárez Rojas]], also known as ''[[Mono Jojoy]]'', on 23 September 2010. President Juan Manuel Santos stated that the FARC commander was killed in an operation that began in the early hours of 21 September in the department of Meta, {{convert|200|mi}} south of the capital Bogotá.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2010-09-24/top-colombian-farc-rebel-killed/2272090 |title=Top Colombian FARC rebel killed |date=24 September 2010 |work=ABC News |access-date=25 September 2011 |archive-date=13 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113104718/http://www.abc.net.au/news/2010-09-24/top-colombian-farc-rebel-killed/2272090 |url-status=live }}</ref> According to Santos, he was "the impersonation of terror and a symbol of violence".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://colombiareports.com/santos-congratules-armed-forces-on-mono-jojoy-death/ |title=Santos congratulates armed forces on death of 'Mono Jojoy' |first=Adriaan |last=Alsema |date=23 September 2010 |work=Colombia Reports |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806182958/https://colombiareports.com/santos-congratules-armed-forces-on-mono-jojoy-death/ |url-status=live }}</ref> After this event, the FARC–EP released a statement saying that defeating the group would not bring peace to Colombia and called for a negotiated solution, not surrender, to the social and political conflict.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://colombiareports.com/farc-we-want-peace-not-surrender/ |title=FARC calls for peace after 'Mono Jojoy' death |first=Teresa |last=Welsh |date=24 September 2010 |work=Colombia Reports |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=16 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016031721/http://colombiareports.com/farc-we-want-peace-not-surrender/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 2011 Juan Manuel Santos admitted that FARC–EP had killed 460 government soldiers and wounded over 2,000 in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elespectador.com/noticias/judicial/articulo-241495-santos-revela-unos-460-militares-y-policias-han-muerto-combate-201 |title=Santos revela que unos 460 militares y policías han muerto en combate en 2010 |work=[[El Espectador]] |language=es |date=2010-12-20 |access-date=15 October 2012 |archive-date=25 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130925182752/http://www.elespectador.com/noticias/judicial/articulo-241495-santos-revela-unos-460-militares-y-policias-han-muerto-combate-201 |url-status=live }}</ref> In April 2011 the Colombian congress issued a statement saying that FARC has a "strong presence" in roughly one third of the municipalities in Colombia, while their attacks have increased.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://elespectador.com/noticias/politica/articulo-265894-alertan-mas-de-330-municipios-tienen-fuerte-presencia-de-farc |title=Alertan que más de 330 municipios tienen fuerte presencia de las FARC |work=El Espectador |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |date=2011-04-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930151055/http://elespectador.com/noticias/politica/articulo-265894-alertan-mas-de-330-municipios-tienen-fuerte-presencia-de-farc |archive-date=30 September 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Overall FARC operations, including attacks against security forces as well as kidnappings and the use of land mines, have increased every year since 2005.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://foreignpolicy.com/articles/2011/07/26/rumble_in_the_jungle |title=Rumble in the Jungle |first=Elizabeth |last=Dickinson |date=26 July 2011 |magazine=Foreign Policy |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-date=12 September 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110912165001/http://www.foreignpolicy.com/articles/2011/07/26/rumble_in_the_jungle |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the first six months of 2011 the FARC carried out an estimated 1,115 actions, which constitutes a 10% increase over the same period in 2010.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.elpais.com.co/elpais/judicial/acciones-den-farc-son-por-debilitamiento-estrategia-santos |title=Acciones de las FARC no son por debilitamiento de estrategia de Santos |date=17 July 2011 |work=[[El País (Cali)|El País]] |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126222643/http://www.elpais.com.co/elpais/judicial/acciones-den-farc-son-por-debilitamiento-estrategia-santos |archive-date=26 January 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

By early 2011 Colombian authorities and news media reported that the FARC and the clandestine sister groups had partly shifted strategy from guerrilla warfare to "a war of militias", meaning that they were increasingly operating in civilian clothes while hiding amongst sympathizers in the civilian population.<ref name="elcolombiano">{{cite web |url=http://www.elcolombiano.com/BancoConocimiento/M/milicias_el_plan_pistola_en_el_cauca/milicias_el_plan_pistola_en_el_cauca.asp |title=Milicias, el plan pistola en el Cauca |first=Javier Alexander |last=Macías |date=9 April 2011 |work=[[El Colombiano]] |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-date=30 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110830145638/http://www.elcolombiano.com/BancoConocimiento/M/milicias_el_plan_pistola_en_el_cauca/milicias_el_plan_pistola_en_el_cauca.asp |url-status=live }}</ref> In early January 2011 the Colombian army said that the FARC has some 18,000 members, with 9,000 of those forming part of the militias.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.enlatino.com/farc-tienen-menos-integrantes-y-estan-debilitadas-dice-jefe-militar-colombiano-26265 |title=FARC tienen menos integrantes y están debilitadas, dice jefe militar colombiano |work=enLatino.com |access-date=17 October 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313022958/http://www.enlatino.com/farc-tienen-menos-integrantes-y-estan-debilitadas-dice-jefe-militar-colombiano-26265 |archive-date=13 March 2012}}</ref> The army says it has identified at least 1,400 such militia members in the FARC strongholds of [[Valle del Cauca]] and [[Cauca Department|Cauca]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rcnradio.com/noticias/09-04-11/fuerzas-militares-tienen-identificados-1410-milicianos-de-las-farc |title=Fuerzas Militares tienen identificados a 1410 milicianos de Las FARC |work=RCN La Radio |access-date=17 October 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118211328/http://www.rcnradio.com/noticias/09-04-11/fuerzas-militares-tienen-identificados-1410-milicianos-de-las-farc |archive-date=18 January 2012}}</ref> In June 2011 Colombian chief of staff Edgar Cely claimed that the FARC wants to "urbanize their actions",<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/ARTICULO-WEB-NEW_NOTA_INTERIOR-9547384.html |title=Reconocer el conflicto no cambia estatus de las FARC – Noticias de Justicia en Colombia |work=El Tiempo |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111145800/http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/ARTICULO-WEB-NEW_NOTA_INTERIOR-9547384.html |archive-date=11 January 2012}}</ref> which could partly explain the increased guerrilla activity in Medellín and particularly Cali.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caracol.com.co/nota.aspx?id=1482785 |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20171012040211/http://caracol.com.co/radio/2011/06/02/regional/1306999440_482785.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-10-12 |title=Acción propagandística de las FARC en Medellín |work=Caracol Radio |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |date=2011-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caracol.com.co/nota.aspx?id=1481191 |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20171012040214/http://caracol.com.co/radio/2011/05/30/judicial/1306773900_481191.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-10-12 |title=Asesinan a dos candidatos a la alcaldía de Campamento en Antioquia |work=Caracol Radio |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |date=2011-05-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.caracol.com.co/nota.aspx?id=1479711 |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20171012040528/http://caracol.com.co/radio/2011/05/27/judicial/1306483560_479711.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2017-10-12 |title=Las FARC amenazan a la senadora antioqueña Liliana Rendón |work=Caracol Radio |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |date=2011-05-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.elespectador.com/noticias/judicial/articulo-272781-hallan-caleta-213-minas-de-farc-cali |title=Hallan caleta con 213 minas de las FARC en Cali |work=El Espectador |language=es |date=26 May 2011 |access-date=17 October 2011 |archive-date=11 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111171237/http://www.elespectador.com/noticias/judicial/articulo-272781-hallan-caleta-213-minas-de-farc-cali |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/policia-dice-que-farc-preparaban-atentado-en-cali_8995482-4 |title=Atentados de las FARC en el Valle – Noticias de Justicia en Colombia |work=El Tiempo |language=es |access-date=17 October 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111145950/http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/policia-dice-que-farc-preparaban-atentado-en-cali_8995482-4 |archive-date=11 January 2012}}</ref> Jeremy McDermott, co-director of Insight Crime, estimates that FARC may have some 30,000 'part-time fighters' in 2011, consisting of both armed and unarmed civilian supporters making up the rebel militia network, instead of full-time fighters wearing uniforms.<ref name="elcolombiano"/><ref>{{cite magazine |last=Otis |first=John |url=http://www.time.com/time/world/article/0,8599,2082791,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716205435/http://www.time.com/time/world/article/0,8599,2082791,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=16 July 2011 |title=Colombia's Guerrillas: The Rebellion That Would Not Die |magazine=[[TIME]] |date=16 July 2011 |access-date=17 October 2011}}</ref>

According to [[Corporación Nuevo Arco Iris]], FARC–EP killed 429 members of the Colombian government's security forces between January and October 2011. During this same period, the rebel group lost 316 of its own members. The year 2011 saw over 2,000 incidents of FARC activity, which was the highest figure recorded since 1998. The NGO has stated that while most of these incidents remain defensive in nature and were not like the large offensives from years past, FARC actions grew since 2005, and the rebel group was carrying out intense operations against small and medium-sized Colombian military units in vulnerable areas.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nuevoarcoiris.org.co/sac/files/oca/informes/Info_EJECUTIVO_2011.pdf |title=Info Ejecutivo 2011 |work=Nuevo Arcoiris |language=es |access-date=14 October 2012}} {{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

Colombian troops killed FARC leader [[Alfonso Cano]] in a firefight on 4 November 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/06/world/americas/alfonso-cano-dead-but-farc-dangerous-analysts-say.html |work=The New York Times |first=Simon |last=Romero |title=Colombian Rebels Still Dangerous Despite Leader's Death |date=5 November 2011 |access-date=7 February 2017 |archive-date=3 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103193349/http://www.nytimes.com/2011/11/06/world/americas/alfonso-cano-dead-but-farc-dangerous-analysts-say.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The 6th Front of the FARC, which was in charge of Cano's security at the time of his death, retaliated by killing two policemen in Suarez and Jambaló some 24 hours after the death of Cano.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.elpais.com.co/elpais/judicial/noticias/nuevo-golpe-farc-abatidos-ocho-guerrilleros-en-meta |title=Un policia muria en combate con las FARC en Cauca, tras muerte de Alfonso Cano |work=El País |language=es |access-date=10 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126222607/http://www.elpais.com.co/elpais/judicial/noticias/nuevo-golpe-farc-abatidos-ocho-guerrilleros-en-meta |archive-date=26 January 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> After the death of Alfonso Cano, [[Timoleón Jiménez]], nicknamed [[Timochenko]], took over the FARC–EP leadership.<ref>{{cite news |title=FARC appoints 'Timochenko' as new supreme leader |url=http://colombiareports.co/farc-appoints-timochenko-as-new-supreme-leader/ |agency=Colombia Reports |date=15 November 2011 |access-date=15 November 2011}}</ref>

On 26 November 2011, the FARC killed Police Captain Edgar Yesid Duarte Valero, Police Lieutenant Elkin Hernández Rivas, Army Corporal Libio José Martínez Estrada, and Police [[Intendant]] Álvaro Moreno after government troops approached the guerrilla camp where they were held in an area of the Caqueta department. Police Sergeant Luis Alberto Erazo Maya managed to escape his captors and was later rescued.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-15905488 |title=Colombia FARC rebels kill four hostages as one escapes |date=27 November 2011 |work=BBC News |access-date=21 June 2018 |archive-date=2 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181102171012/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-15905488 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The Colombian military had information indicating that there could be captives in the area and initiated Operation Jupiter in October 2011, using a 56 men Special Forces unit to carry out surveillance for preparing a future rescue mission that would involve additional troops and air support. According to the Colombian military, this same unit remained in the area for 43 days and did not find the captives until they accidentally ran into the FARC camp on the way back, which led to a shootout.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/ARTICULO-WEB-NEW_NOTA_INTERIOR-10844484.html |work=El Tiempo |title=Así fue la operación Júpiter donde murieron los cuatro militares |date=28 November 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130511154756/http://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/ARTICULO-WEB-NEW_NOTA_INTERIOR-10844484.html |archive-date=11 May 2013}}</ref> Relatives of the captives, former victims and civil society groups blamed both the government and FARC for the outcome, questioning the operation as well as criticizing military rescues.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.elmundo.es/america/2011/11/26/colombia/1322341418.html |work=El Mundo |title=Clamor en Colombia contra los 'rescates a sangre y fuego' |date=26 November 2011 |language=es}}</ref>

==== 2012–2015: Peace talks and end of the armed conflict ====
{{See also|Colombian peace process}}
In 2012, FARC announced they would no longer participate in kidnappings for ransom and released the last ten soldiers and police officers they kept as prisoners, but it has kept silent about the status of hundreds of civilians still reported as hostages, and continued kidnapping soldiers and civilians.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/apr/03/colombian-farc-releases-hostages-jungle |title=Colombian FARC rebels release hostages after decade of jungle captivity |first=Toby |last=Muse |date=3 April 2012 |work=The Guardian |access-date=14 October 2012 |location=London}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/features/2012/05/20125301425187352.html |title=FARC's civilian captives suffer in silence |first=Gabriel |last=Elizondo |date=31 May 2012 |work=Al Jazeera English |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=5 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005091908/http://www.aljazeera.com/indepth/features/2012/05/20125301425187352.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 26 February 2012, the FARC announced that they would release their remaining ten political hostages.<ref>{{cite news |title=FARC announces intention to release all hostages, abandon kidnapping |url=https://colombiareports.com/farc-announces-to-release-all-hostages-abandon-kidnapping/ |access-date=4 April 2012 |newspaper=Colombia Reports |date=26 February 2012 |archive-date=3 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003011917/http://colombiareports.com/farc-announces-to-release-all-hostages-abandon-kidnapping/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The hostages were released on 2 April 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=FARC releases all political hostages |url=https://colombiareports.com/farc-releases-all-political-hostages-red-cross/ |access-date=4 April 2012 |work=Colombia Reports |date=2 April 2012}}</ref> The president of Colombia, [[Juan Manuel Santos]], said that this incident was "not enough", and asked the FARC to release the civilian hostages they possess.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ramsey |first=Geoffrey |title=FARC Release Hostages, Though Hundreds of Civilians Remain Kidnapped |url=http://insightcrime.org/insight-latest-news/item/2438-farc-release-hostages-though-hundreds-of-civilians-remain-kidnapped |newspaper=Insight Crime |date=3 April 2012 |access-date=18 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406013339/http://www.insightcrime.org/insight-latest-news/item/2438-farc-release-hostages-though-hundreds-of-civilians-remain-kidnapped |archive-date=6 April 2012}}</ref>

On 22 November 2012, the FARC released four Chinese oil workers. The hostages were working for the Emerald Energy oil company, a British-based subsidiary of China's Sinochem Group, when they were kidnapped on 8 June 2011. Their Colombian driver was also kidnapped, but released several hours later. Authorities identified the freed men as Tang Guofu, Zhao Hongwei, Jian Mingfu, and Jiang Shan.<ref name="boston">{{cite news |url=https://www.boston.com/news/world/latin-america/2012/11/22/chinese-oil-workers-freed-colombian-rebels/sQTr3I90wnzsxJ7BY1XbNM/story.html |title=4 Chinese oil workers freed by Colombian rebels |work=Boston.com |access-date=11 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121130045814/http://www.boston.com/news/world/latin-america/2012/11/22/chinese-oil-workers-freed-colombian-rebels/sQTr3I90wnzsxJ7BY1XbNM/story.html |archive-date=30 November 2012}}</ref><ref name="google">{{cite web |url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/afp/article/ALeqM5g1WW264DSf9G5ngUUCQP3zwM-R7w?docId=CNG.2fcb1efab89358c96050cee9ce6108a5.171&hl=en |title=Four Chinese hostages freed in Colombia |work=AFP |access-date=11 January 2014 |via=Google News}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Santos announced on 27 August 2012 that the Colombian government has engaged in talks with FARC in order to seek an end to the conflict:<ref name="elnaljaz">{{cite web |author=Inside Story Americas |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/programmes/insidestoryamericas/2012/08/201283010395107836.html |title=Is Colombia's conflict coming to an end? |work=Al Jazeera English |date=30 August 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=24 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924071026/http://www.aljazeera.com/programmes/insidestoryamericas/2012/08/201283010395107836.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

<blockquote>Exploratory conversations have been held with the FARC to find an end to the conflict. I want to make very clear to Colombians that the approaches that have been carried out and the ones that will happen in the future will be carried out within the framework based on these principles: We are going to learn from the mistakes made in the past so that they are not repeated. Second, any process must lead to the end of the conflict, not making it longer. Third, operations and military presence will be maintained across the entire national territory.</blockquote>

He also said that he would learn from the mistakes of previous leaders, who failed to secure a lasting ceasefire with FARC, though the military would still continue operations throughout Colombia while talks continued.<ref name="Colombia peace Yahoo">{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.com/colombian-government-seeking-peace-farce-rebels-021300909.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121023061133/http://news.yahoo.com/colombian-government-seeking-peace-farce-rebels-021300909.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 October 2012 |title=Colombian government seeking peace with FARC rebels |work=Yahoo! News |agency=Reuters |date=27 August 2012 |access-date=28 August 2012 |author1=Murphy, Helen |author2=Acosta, Luis James}}</ref> An unnamed Colombian intelligence source said Santos has assured FARC that no one would be extradited to stand trial in another country.<ref name="France 24 peace">{{cite web |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20120827-colombia-government-talks-raise-prospect-farc-peace-deal-alvaro-uribe-santos |title=Government, FARC rebels agree to peace talks |work=France 24 |agency=Reuters |date=27 August 2012 |access-date=28 August 2012 |archive-date=28 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120828130126/http://www.france24.com/en/20120827-colombia-government-talks-raise-prospect-farc-peace-deal-alvaro-uribe-santos |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Al Jazeera'' reported that the initiative began after Santos met with Venezuelan President [[Hugo Chávez]] and asked him to mediate. Former President Uribe has criticized Santos for seeking peace "at any cost" and rejected the idea of holding talks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2012/08/20128280155953340.html |title=Colombia seeking peace with FARC rebels |work=Al Jazeera English |date=29 August 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=1 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180801031548/https://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2012/08/20128280155953340.html |url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[TeleSUR|Telesur]]'' reported that FARC and the Colombian government had signed a preliminary agreement in [[Havana]] the same day. The first round of the talks will take place in [[Oslo]] on 5 October and then return to Havana<ref name="BBC peace">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-19393096 |title=Colombia agrees to hold peace talks with FARC rebels |work=BBC News |date=27 August 2012 |access-date=28 August 2012 |archive-date=28 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120828092939/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-19393096 |url-status=live }}</ref>{{update after|2012|10|05}} for approximately six months of talks before culminating in Colombia.<ref name="tbo"/> However, Santos later ruled out a ceasefire pending the talks in Oslo and reiterated that offensive operations against FARC would continue.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2012/09/2012975934866866.html |title=Colombia rules out ceasefire with FARC |work=Al Jazeera English |date=7 September 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012}}</ref>

ELN leader Nicolás Rodríguez Bautista, otherwise known as Gabino, added that his group was interested in joining the talks too: "Well we are open, it's exactly our proposal, to seek room for open dialogue without conditions and start to discuss the nation's biggest problems. But the government has said no! Santos says he has the keys to peace in his pocket, but I think he has lost them because there seems to be no possibility of a serious dialogue, we remain holding out for that."<ref name="elnaljaz"/>

Colombia's [[RCN Radio]] reported on 29 September<ref name="Colombia peace RCN">{{cite web |url=http://www.rcnradio.com/noticias/puntos-del-acuerdo-de-negociacion-entre-gobierno-y-farc-18177 |title=Puntos del acuerdo de negociación entre Gobierno y FARC |work=RCN Radio |date=29 August 2012 |language=es |access-date=9 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120831195503/http://www.rcnradio.com/noticias/puntos-del-acuerdo-de-negociacion-entre-gobierno-y-farc-18177 |archive-date=31 August 2012}}</ref> that a preliminary draft of the proposals<ref name="Colombia peace Colombia Reports">{{cite web |url=https://colombiareports.com/agreement-colombia-government-and-rebel-group-farc/ |title=Text of deal between Colombia's government and rebel group FARC to end armed conflict |work=Colombia Reports |date=29 August 2012 |access-date=9 October 2012 |archive-date=1 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501001042/http://colombiareports.com/agreement-colombia-government-and-rebel-group-farc/ |url-status=live }}</ref> indicated that a resolution would involve answering FARC's historic grievances including rural development and agrarian reform; democracy development via an enhancement of the number of registered political parties; security and compensation for the victims of the conflict. In these regards, the Colombian government has already passed a series of laws that entail compensation for the victims and a return of land to the displaced. FARC also indicated a willingness to give up their arms. Former [[19 April Movement|M19]] member [[Antonio Navarro Wolff]] said: "If the government wants a serious peace plan they will have to take control of the coca leaf plantations that are currently owned by the FARC because if not another criminal group will take over it."<ref name="tbo">{{cite web |url=http://blogs.aljazeera.com/blog/americas/stage-set-colombias-peace-process |title=Stage set for Colombia's peace process |work=Al Jazeera |date=3 September 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=11 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120911063939/http://blogs.aljazeera.com/blog/americas/stage-set-colombias-peace-process |url-status=dead}}</ref> Santos later told ''Al Jazeera'' that peace was possible if there was "goodwill" on both sides.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2012/09/20129816352348815.html |title=Colombia's Santos believes peace is possible |work=Al Jazeera English |date=9 September 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=3 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121003191829/http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2012/09/20129816352348815.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Santos told the [[General debate of the sixty-seventh session of the United Nations General Assembly]] on 26 September, that Venezuela and Chile were also helping in the discussion along with Cuba and Norway.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gadebate.un.org/67/colombia |title=UN General Assembly General Debate of the 67th Session – Colombia |work=GA Debate.un.org |date=26 September 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=30 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930025024/http://gadebate.un.org/67/colombia |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://gadebate.un.org/67/venezuela-bolivarian-republic |title=UN General Assembly General Debate of the 67th Session – Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) |work=GA Debate.un.org |date=1 October 2012 |access-date=14 October 2012 |archive-date=5 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005051539/http://gadebate.un.org/67/venezuela-bolivarian-republic |url-status=live }}</ref>

Peace talks were formally started on 18 October in a hotel 30 miles north of the Norwegian capital [[Oslo]] with a joint-press conference by both delegations.<ref name="Colombia peace Colombia Reports 2">{{cite web |url=https://colombiareports.com/colombia-govt-rebels-begin-serious-dignified-and-efficientq-peace-process/ |title=Colombia govt, rebels begin 'serious, dignified and efficient' peace process |work=Colombia Reports |date=18 October 2012 |access-date=18 October 2012 |archive-date=23 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523133535/http://colombiareports.com/colombia-govt-rebels-begin-serious-dignified-and-efficientq-peace-process/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The representatives of the government, led by [[Humberto de la Calle]] and the FARC, led by [[Iván Márquez]], said the so-called second phase of the peace process will be inaugurated in Oslo on 15 November, after which the delegations will go to Cuba to work on the negotiation of the peace accord, which will ultimately lead to a permanent agreement and [[ceasefire]]. The Colombian government has also stated that they expect that a post-Chávez government will continue to support the peace process. In late 2012, FARC declared a two-month unilateral cease-fire and said that they would be open to extending it as a bilateral truce afterwards during the rest of the negotiations. The Colombian government refused to agree to a bilateral cease-fire, alleging violations of the truce by FARC.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-chavez-santos-idUSBRE90E0SC20130115 |title=Colombia expects Venezuelan help for FARC talks even if Chavez dies |work=Reuters |date=15 January 2013 |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728133609/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-chavez-santos-idUSBRE90E0SC20130115 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2013/01/201312016575695697.html |title=Colombia refuses to extend FARC ceasefire |work=Al Jazeera |date=20 January 2013 |access-date=23 January 2014 |archive-date=30 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140130185143/http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2013/01/201312016575695697.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Shortly after lifting the ceasefire, FARC conducted attacks on a coal transport railway, which derailed 17 wagons and forced a suspension of operations<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.coalguru.com/south_america/farc_attacks_coal_railway_in_north_colombia/8131 |title=FARC attacks coal railway in North Colombia |work=Coalguru.com |access-date=23 January 2014 |archive-date=28 June 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130628220622/http://www.coalguru.com/south_america/farc_attacks_coal_railway_in_north_colombia/8131 |url-status=live }}</ref> and assaulted [[Milán, Caquetá]], a town in the southern [[Caquetá Department|Caquetá]], killing at least seven government soldiers and injuring five others.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/14/world/americas/colombia-soldiers-die-in-rebel-fight.html |title=Colombia: Soldiers Die in Rebel Fight |date=14 February 2013 |work=The New York Times |agency=Associated Press |access-date=7 February 2017 |archive-date=13 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170113091702/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/14/world/americas/colombia-soldiers-die-in-rebel-fight.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Santos has been far more responsive to threats against social leaders than his predecessors. He has also been decisive in combatting the New Illegal Armed Groups that emerged as a result of the [[paramilitary]] process, especially in fighting threats and violence against human rights defenders and social leaders. During Santos' presidency, private security and proclaimed self-defense movements have also lost their legitimacy.<ref name="CrisisGroup.org"/>

On 27 May 2013, it was announced that one of the most contentious issues had been resolved. Land reform and compensation was tackled with promises to compensate those who had lost land.<ref name="aljazeera">{{cite web |url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2013/05/2013526182915832728.html |title=Deal reached on land reform in Colombia |date=27 May 2013 |work=Al Jazeera |access-date=11 January 2014 |archive-date=30 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140130185139/http://www.aljazeera.com/news/americas/2013/05/2013526182915832728.html |url-status=live }}</ref> This is the first time the government and FARC have reached an agreement on a substantive issue in four different negotiating attempts over 30 years. The peace process then moved on to the issue of "political participation", during which FARC insisted on its demand for an elected Constituent Assembly to rewrite Colombia's constitution. This demand has been forcefully rejected by Colombia's lead government negotiator, Humberto de la Calle.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/de-calle-dice-no-farc-por-que/346491-3 |title=De la Calle le dice NO a las FARC. ¿Por qué? |date=15 June 2013 |magazine=[[Semana]] |language=es |access-date=1 August 2013 |archive-date=23 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723021506/http://www.semana.com/nacion/articulo/de-calle-dice-no-farc-por-que/346491-3 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 20 June 2013, FARC kidnapped American tourist Kevin Scott Sutay. He was released on 27 October 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/colombian-rebels-free-kidnapped-former-us-marine-kevin-scott-sutay-flna8C11477352|title=Colombian rebels free kidnapped former US Marine Kevin Scott Sutay|date=27 October 2013|website=NBC News}}</ref>

On 1 July 2013, FARC and the second-largest guerrilla group in Colombia, ELN, announced that they would be working together to find a "political solution to the social and armed conflict." The details of this partnership, however, were far from clear; [[Washington Office on Latin America]]'s Adam Isacson explains that two issues central to peace accords with ELN—resource policy and kidnapping—are currently off the table in the talks in Havana with FARC, and the addition of these topics may complicate and slow down an already sluggish process.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://colombiapeace.org/2013/07/16/colombia-peace-process-update-july-15-2013/ |title=Colombia Peace Process Update |first=Adam |last=Isacson |date=16 July 2013 |website=ColombiaPeace.org |access-date=1 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130717160605/http://colombiapeace.org/2013/07/16/colombia-peace-process-update-july-15-2013/ |archive-date=17 July 2013}}</ref>

On 6 November 2013 the Colombian government and FARC announced that they had come to an agreement regarding the participation of political opposition and would begin discussing their next issue, the illicit drug trade.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mesadeconversaciones.com.co/comunicados/comunicado-conjunto-la-habana-noviembre-6-de-2013?ver=es |title=Comunicado Conjunto. La Habana, 06 de Noviembre de 2013 |date=6 November 2013 |work=Mesa de Conversaciones para la Terminación del Conflicto y la Construcción de una Paz Estable y Duradera en Colombia |language=es |access-date=20 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512221119/https://www.mesadeconversaciones.com.co/comunicados/comunicado-conjunto-la-habana-noviembre-6-de-2013?ver=es |archive-date=12 May 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 23 January 2014 Juan Fernando Cristo, the President of the Senate of Colombia, proposed a second [[Plan Colombia]] during a conference on the Colombian peace process in Washington, D.C.<ref name="lanacion.com.co">{{cite news |title=Cristo propuso Plan Colombia II para postconflicto y reparación de víctimas |url=http://www.lanacion.com.co/index.php/politica/item/229036-cristo-propuso-plan-colombia-ii-para-postconflicto-y-reparacion-de-victimas |date=23 January 2014 |newspaper=La Nación |access-date=20 February 2014 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150904014414/http://www.lanacion.com.co/index.php/politica/item/229036-cristo-propuso-plan-colombia-ii-para-postconflicto-y-reparacion-de-victimas |archive-date=4 September 2015}}</ref> Cristo stated that this new plan should be "for the victims" and should redirect the resources from the original Plan Colombia towards supporting a post-conflict Colombia.<ref name="lanacion.com.co"/>

On 16 May 2014, the Colombian government and the FARC rebels agreed to work together against drug trafficking, added to the development of these peace talks.<ref name="nytimes">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/17/world/americas/colombia-and-rebels-agree-on-drug-fight.html?ref=americas |title=Colombia and Rebels Agree on Drug Fight |newspaper=The New York Times |access-date=28 June 2014 |date=2014-05-16 |last1=Neuman |first1=William}}</ref><ref name="reuters">{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-rebels-idUSBREA4F0CE20140516 |title=Colombian government, rebels move closer to peace deal |work=Reuters |access-date=28 June 2014 |date=2014-05-16 |archive-date=29 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140529034424/http://www.reuters.com/article/2014/05/16/us-colombia-rebels-idUSBREA4F0CE20140516 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 June 2015, humanitarian and spiritual leader [[Ravi Shankar (spiritual leader)|Ravi Shankar]], on a three-day-visit to Cuba, had several rounds of discussions with FARC members in an exercise of confidence-building in the peace process, which had many hurdles from the past three years.

FARC requested Shankar to actively participate in the peace process. He said, "In this conflict, everyone should be considered as victims. And inside every culprit, there is a victim crying for help."

After many discussions, FARC finally agreed to embrace the Gandhian principle of non-violence. Commander Ivan Marquez declared in the press conference that they would adopt it. The FARC agreed that hatred had derailed the peace process. Marquez said, "We will work for peace and justice for all the people of Colombia."<ref>{{cite news |title=Sri Sri Ravi Shankar convinces guerrilla movement FARC to adopt Gandhian principles |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2015-06-29/news/63937874_1_sri-sri-ravi-shankar-peace-talks-colombia |access-date=14 October 2015 |newspaper=[[The Economic Times]] |date=29 June 2015 |archive-date=16 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016031716/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2015-06-29/news/63937874_1_sri-sri-ravi-shankar-peace-talks-colombia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 8 July 2015, FARC announced a unilateral ceasefire, which began on 20 July 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-33450816 |title=Colombia FARC rebels call unilateral ceasefire |work=BBC News |date=8 July 2015 |access-date=22 September 2015 |archive-date=16 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016031716/http://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-33450816 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/jul/08/farc-rebels-unilateral-ceasefire-colombia-peace-talks |title=FARC rebels announce unilateral truce in attempt to rescue Colombia peace talks |newspaper=The Guardian |date=8 July 2015 |access-date=22 September 2015 |last1=Brodzinsky |first1=Sibylla}}</ref>

On 30 September 2015, Ravi Shankar accused Norway of sidetracking his effort at brokering a peace deal between the Colombian government and FARC, after Norway, which was part of a four-nation group (along with Cuba, Chile and Venezuela) acting as guarantors in the talks, released a statement saying that the peace deal was a result of "painstaking efforts undertaken by a league of Western nations".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Guha Ray |first1=Shantanu |title=Sri Sri Ravi Shankar miffed with the Pope |url=http://www.mid-day.com/articles/sri-sri-ravi-shankar-miffed-with-the-pope/16571168 |access-date=1 October 2015 |work=[[Mid-Day]] |date=30 September 2015 |archive-date=1 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001171709/http://www.mid-day.com/articles/sri-sri-ravi-shankar-miffed-with-the-pope/16571168 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== 2016–2017: Ceasefire and disarming ====
On 23 June 2016 a ceasefire accord was signed between the FARC Guerilla Army and the Colombian Government, in [[Havana]], Cuba. Leaders of several Latin American countries which contributed to the deal, including Cuba and Venezuela, were present. The final peace accord [[2016 Colombian peace agreement referendum|required a referendum]] to be approved.<ref>{{cite news |title=Colombia and FARC rebels sign historic ceasefire deal to end 50-year conflict |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/jun/23/colombia-farc-rebel-ceasefire-agreement-havana |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=24 June 2016 |date=2016-06-23 |last1=Brodzinsky |first1=Sibylla |last2=Watts |first2=Jonathan |archive-date=24 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160624120025/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/jun/23/colombia-farc-rebel-ceasefire-agreement-havana |url-status=live }}</ref>

Under the accord, the Colombian government will support massive investment for rural development and facilitate the FARC's reincarnation as a legal political party. FARC promised to help eradicate illegal drug crops, remove landmines in the areas of conflict, and offer reparations to victims. FARC leaders can avoid prosecution by acts of reparation to victims and other community work.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rural Colombians hope 'pretty promises' can bring peace back to paradise |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2016/jun/23/colombia-peace-deal-civilians-farc-guerrillas |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=24 June 2016 |date=2016-06-23 |last1=Brodzinsky |first1=Sibylla}}</ref>

On 2 October 2016 Colombians voted and rejected the peace deal with FARC by 50.2% to 49.8%.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://thecitypaperbogota.com/news/no-wins-colombians-narrowly-rejects-peace-accord-with-farc/14639 |title="No" wins plebiscite: Colombians reject FARC peace accord |last=Emblin |first=Richard |date=2016-10-02 |work=The City Paper Bogotá |access-date=18 May 2020 |archive-date=11 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411090705/http://thecitypaperbogota.com/news/no-wins-colombians-narrowly-rejects-peace-accord-with-farc/14639 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The government met with victims and peace opponents after the referendum was rejected, receiving over 500 proposed changes, and continued to negotiate with FARC.<ref name="ET 1">{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz-entre-el-gobierno-y-las-farc/16749079 |title=De la Calle y Márquez anunciaron desde Cuba nuevo texto de negociación |language=es |trans-title=De la Calle and Márquez announced from Cuba new negotiation text |newspaper=[[El Tiempo (Colombia)|El Tiempo]] |date=2016-11-12 |access-date=2016-11-12 |archive-date=13 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113181220/http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz-entre-el-gobierno-y-las-farc/16749079 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/santos-habla-sobre-nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz/16749160 |title='Se logró un nuevo acuerdo que ahora es de todos': Santos |newspaper=El Tiempo |language=es |access-date=2016-11-12 |date=2016-11-12 |archive-date=13 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113181446/http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/santos-habla-sobre-nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz/16749160 |url-status=live }}</ref> A revised agreement announced on 12 November 2016, which would require parliamentary approval rather than a nationwide referendum.<ref name="bbc deal">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-37965392 |title=Colombia peace deal: Government and FARC reach new agreement |work=BBC News |date=2016-11-12 |access-date=2016-11-12 |archive-date=16 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616002825/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-37965392 |url-status=live }}</ref> Former President and chief peace opponent [[Álvaro Uribe]] met with President [[Juan Manuel Santos]] and thereafter issued a noncommittal statement that he awaited release of the full text. Among the reported 60 new or modified terms was a provision for FARC assets to be distributed for victim compensation.<ref name="ET 1"/> FARC members would be able to establish a political party, and would in general be granted full immunity for full confession and cooperation, although drug trafficking would be assessed on a case-by-case basis. Peace terms would be enforced by a Special Justice for the Peace, who would report to the Constitutional Court and not to an international body, and both Parliament and the Special Justice would have the ability to modify the terms of the agreement as seen necessary.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/los-cambios-que-trae-el-nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz/16749153 |title=Cinco claves para entender el nuevo acuerdo de La Habana |language=es |trans-title=Five keys to understand the new agreement from Havana |newspaper=El Tiempo |access-date=2016-11-12 |date=2016-11-12 |archive-date=13 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113180530/http://www.eltiempo.com/politica/proceso-de-paz/los-cambios-que-trae-el-nuevo-acuerdo-de-paz/16749153 |url-status=live }}</ref>
